issues.claim: §3.2 (9) runs '(b) when the arena grows, (a) and (c) when the frame grows' (l. 3639–3640) and states the frame record's replacement only inside (b): '`Plat.frame` takes the new frame as its last batch commits' (l. 3652). The new arena is 'the new frame plus the current law's margin, kept at the current arena where that is no larger …' (l. 3631–3633), a change of frame law included (l. 3635–3636), so a growth at a change of law can grow the frame and keep the arena. Reachable: a TOWN made at 9 000 people (base law 7.2 km², a 2 683 m square; arena 4 293 m) handed down to the village product below 1 425 (V07 §2.1; frame and arena kept), falling below 400 (HAMLET) and re-crossing 400: the VILLAGE row's territory law (V07 §3.2 (1)) gives 11.375 km², a 3 373 m square (the frame grows 345 m a side), while 3 373 × 1.2 = 4 047 m < 4 293 m keeps the arena. Only (a) and (c) run: the text never says when Plat.frame takes the new frame, and the new Frame's marginShare (the law's 0.1 by the record's comment, l. 3562) breaks 'the arena spans the frame plus marginShare on every side' (l. 3621) by 123 m a side. A builder who updates Plat.frame in (b)'s step, as the text places it, leaves it at 2 683 m under a 3 373 m border: the zoom-out limit's bounds (§8.8 DisplayList.bounds; V07 W79, T-V7-64) do not move, and at the hand-off up (1 575 people, TOWN law 1.26 km², frame kept) the arena from the stale frame is 4 293 m (nothing runs) where the stated design grows it to 3 373 × 1.6 = 5 397 m by (b). Two builders, two behaviours on a defined epoch path (principle (11)); repair-r4-kernel.md's observation 1, confirmed; it predates round 4.

(2) The `Frame` interface's `marginShare` comment, l. 3562: after '`territory.marginShare` under the `territory` law (V07 §3.2 (1))' insert '; the kept arena's own share where an epoch's growth kept a wider arena (§3.2 (9))'.

issues.claim: §13.1's kernel set (l. 17594–17595) grows a frame at a change of law only in 'a village → town fold (the frame kept, the arena by the new law's margin, neither shrinking; §3.2 (9))', the case where only (b) runs. No fixture runs the reverse, where only (a) and (c) run (VKr4-01): T-V7-14's 1 400 / 1 600 alternation never regrows inside the village product, T-V7-64 grows a village's frame under one law, and T81-1 and T110-2 grow across a crossing under one law. An untested edge is a MAJOR (principle (11)).
